title: 1Password reports internal breach, confirms user password vaults remain secure
summary: Password management provider 1Password announced that hackers breached an employee's corporate user account and accessed internal system information. The company emphasized that customer password vaults were not accessed and remain secured by end-to-end encryption.
point1: An attacker compromised a corporate employee account to access internal system data.
point2: Customer password vaults remained uncompromised due to zero-knowledge encryption.
point3: Security reviews and internal remediations are ongoing.

title: Global apparel brands shift $254 million in production from Bangladesh to India
summary: International clothing brands diverted approximately $254 million worth of orders away from Bangladesh during an 18-day period in November due to political unrest. Factory owners reported that the vast majority of the relocated manufacturing orders went to Indian suppliers.
point1: Global brands diverted $254 million in apparel orders from Bangladesh during November.
point2: Indian garment manufacturers captured most of the redirected international contracts.
point3: Order reallocations are ongoing as uncertainty persists in Bangladesh.

title: India-U.S. trade agreement nearing culmination, confirms Piyush Goyal
summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal stated that negotiations for a bilateral trade agreement between India and the United States are nearing finalization. The process follows a USTR report proposing tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, which could be capped at 17% if a deal is reached.
point1: Minister Piyush Goyal confirmed the India-U.S. trade pact pathway is taking final shape.
point2: The deal aims to limit potential U.S. tariffs on Indian exports to 17%.
point3: Final signing details and implementation schedules remain under negotiation.

title: FCC approves SpaceX plan to deploy AI data centers in orbit
summary: The Federal Communications Commission granted approval for SpaceX to deploy artificial intelligence data centers into space orbit. The agency dismissed third-party objections regarding potential impacts on scientific research, ruling that those concerns fall outside its regulatory domain.
point1: The FCC authorized SpaceX to put AI computing infrastructure into space.
point2: The regulatory clearance removes a major legal hurdle for orbital data centers.
point3: No confirmed timeline reported.

title: Indian Cabinet clears Delimitation Bill proposing 850 Lok Sabha seats
summary: The Union Cabinet cleared the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, proposing a 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats up to 850 members. The draft legislation includes provisions for women's seat reservations and a 25-year seat freeze, prompting opposition parties to plan a joint response.
point1: The proposed bill expands the Lok Sabha capacity to 850 seats.
point2: The legislation alters parliamentary representation structure and electoral seat allocations across Indian states.
point3: Opposition leaders are holding joint meetings ahead of the special parliamentary session.

title: Kenyan Doomsday Cult Leader Paul Mackenzie Convicted for 123 Additional Deaths
summary: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie has been found guilty of manslaughter in connection with 123 additional follower deaths in the Shakahola forest. The conviction follows earlier murder sentences linked to the mass starvation deaths of children inside the cult's compound. Authorities continue to prosecute charges stemming from the mass casualty tragedy.
point1: Paul Mackenzie was convicted of manslaughter for 123 additional deaths among his followers.
point2: The verdict follows previous convictions and life prison terms linked to the Shakahola forest deaths.
point3: Sentencing for the latest convictions will be delivered by the court at a later date.

title: Volkswagen Challenges $1.2 Billion Tax Demand in India, Cites Competitor Tariffs in Court
summary: Volkswagen Group is contesting a $1.2 billion tax assessment in Indian court, arguing the penalty threatens its operational viability in the country. In its legal filings, Volkswagen cited import classification standards used by competitors Mercedes-Benz and BMW to dispute the government's targeted claims. Volkswagen holds a two percent market share in India's automotive sector.
point1: Volkswagen is challenging a $1.2 billion tax assessment issued by Indian financial authorities.
point2: The automaker warned that the tax demand could wipe out its long-term investments in India.
point3: Legal proceedings regarding the tax dispute remain ongoing before Indian courts.

title: Indian Navy Completes Project 17A Stealth Frigate Program with Delivery of INS Vindhyagiri
summary: Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers handed over the stealth frigate Vindhyagiri to the Indian Navy, marking the formal completion of the Project 17A warship construction program. Vindhyagiri is the third and final Project 17A frigate constructed by GRSE in Kolkata. The delivery strengthens the navy's frontline surface warfare capabilities.
point1: GRSE handed over Vindhyagiri, completing the build program for Project 17A stealth frigates.
point2: The vessel marks the final ship delivered under GRSE's Project 17A defense mandate.
point3: The warship will undergo final naval commissioning procedures before full operational deployment.

title: Indian Government Introduces Bill to Expand Lok Sabha to 850 Seats and Freeze State Share Until 2051
summary: The Indian government has introduced the 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill alongside a fresh Delimitation Bill to increase Lok Sabha seats in each state by 50 percent, raising the total to 850 seats. The proposed legislation freezes seat proportions among states until 2051, decoupling seat distribution from population stabilization metrics. Additionally, the bills bring into force a 33 percent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha.
point1: The 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill increases Lok Sabha seats by 50% across states and freezes proportional representation until 2051.
point2: The legislation removes the historical linkage between seat allocation freezes and population stabilization goals while bringing women's reservations into effect.
point3: The bills have been formally introduced in Parliament for consideration.

title: EU budget summit stalls over funding disputes and Ukraine assistance
summary: Negotiations among European Union leaders over the bloc's long-term budget have broken down without an agreement. Key disputes center on financial aid packages for Ukraine and broader spending allocations among member states.
point1: EU leaders failed to reach a consensus on the multi-year common budget.
point2: Disagreements over aid to Ukraine and internal national contributions remain unresolved.
point3: EU leaders aim to resolve budget negotiations before the end of the year.

title: Venezuela moves to repeal law barring opposition candidates from public office
summary: Venezuela announced it will scrap legislation used to ban political opposition figures from holding public office. The statute had drawn widespread international condemnation over the past two years for facilitating political persecution.
point1: Venezuela announced plans to repeal laws that disqualified opposition leaders from seeking election.
point2: The change addresses major international demands regarding democratic processes and political bans.
point3: Legislative procedures to formally rescind the measure are expected to follow.

title: Zelensky criticizes US diplomatic strategy and peace negotiations in BBC interview
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed frustration over Washington's diplomatic stance toward Moscow in an interview with the BBC. Zelensky warned that the U.S. is not applying sufficient leverage on Russia during peace talks to end the ongoing war.
point1: Zelensky publicly criticized the U.S. diplomatic posture toward Kremlin peace negotiations.
point2: The Ukrainian leader asserted that soft diplomatic pressure risks compromising Ukraine's security.
point3: Diplomatic efforts and international discussions regarding peace terms are ongoing.

title: Supreme Court orders Thirupparankundram deepam lighting and issues contempt notices
summary: The Supreme Court of India ordered the lighting of the traditional deepam on the 'deepathoon' at Thirupparankundram. Finding that state authorities willfully disobeyed judicial orders, the court issued contempt notices to the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, DGP, and other senior officials.
point1: The Supreme Court mandated that the deepam be lit on November 28.
point2: Show cause notices for contempt were issued against Tamil Nadu's Chief Secretary, DGP, and temple trustees.
point3: The court mandated the lighting ceremony for November 28, 2026.

title: RBI lowers daily CRR maintenance requirement to 90%, releasing over ₹40,000 crore
summary: The Reserve Bank of India reduced the daily minimum Cash Reserve Ratio maintenance requirement for commercial banks to 90%. The liquidity adjustment is projected to unlock more than ₹40,000 crore across the banking system.
point1: The RBI reduced the daily minimum CRR requirement for commercial banks from its previous level to 90%.
point2: The decision releases over ₹40,000 crore into the financial system to support bank liquidity and credit delivery.
point3: The policy change takes effect immediately according to central bank guidelines.

title: New York enacts five-year ban on AI chatbot toys over child safety concerns
summary: New York State has banned AI chatbot toys for five years following safety evaluations from Common Sense Media. Research showed significant vulnerabilities, including exposure to inappropriate content and potential harm to children's emotional development.
point1: New York implemented a five-year prohibition on sales of AI-enabled interactive toys.
point2: The legislative action marks one of the earliest state-level bans specifically targeting child-facing AI software.
point3: The restriction remains active for five years.

title: Affordable HIV prevention drug Lenacapavir reaches African nations
summary: Lenacapavir, a twice-yearly injectable drug with near-100% efficacy in preventing HIV infection, has begun rollout in Africa under reduced-cost agreements. Public health officials anticipate the treatment will dramatically curb transmission rates.
point1: Lenacapavir provides near-100% HIV protection with only two injections per year.
point2: Lowered pricing models enable wide distribution across high-incidence African countries.
point3: No confirmed timeline reported.

title: Two Italian technicians killed in strike in Kuwait
summary: Two Italian technicians working for German defense contractor Rheinmetall were killed during a strike in Kuwait. Italy's foreign ministry confirmed the deaths, while Iranian authorities denied involvement in the attack.
point1: Two Italian defense contractors died following a military strike in Kuwait.
point2: The fatal attack highlights escalating security risks to international defense personnel in the region.
point3: No confirmed timeline reported.

title: New Zealand ruling coalition falls short of parliamentary majority
summary: New Zealand's right-leaning ruling coalition led by the National Party fell short of a parliamentary majority by a single seat. The final election results leave the governing bloc unable to secure an absolute majority independently.
point1: The ruling bloc missed securing a full majority by one seat.
point2: The parliamentary deficit requires the governing coalition to negotiate external support to maintain stability.
point3: No confirmed timeline reported.

title: C-DAC targets indigenous 32,000-core GPU production by mid-2028
summary: The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing announced plans to develop a domestic 32,000-core graphics processing unit by mid-2028. The government organization is seeking commercial partners to transfer its functional FPGA hardware model into silicon manufacturing.
point1: C-DAC initiated a national program to manufacture a 32,000-core indigenous GPU.
point2: The project aims to reduce dependence on foreign hardware providers and boost domestic chip production.
point3: Commercial production is targeted for completion by mid-2028.

title: Supreme Court gives FSSAI four months to enforce stricter food label norms
summary: India's Supreme Court instructed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India to finalize enhanced front-of-package nutrition labeling rules within four months. The court directed that regulations must measure total sugars, saturated fat, and sodium to better protect public health.
point1: The Supreme Court mandated comprehensive front-of-package warning labels on processed foods.
point2: Regulators must focus on total sugar and saturated fat thresholds rather than added ingredients alone.
point3: FSSAI must finalize and issue the updated labeling regulations within four months.

title: NCLAT orders ₹480 crore payout to Jet Airways workers within two weeks
summary: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal ordered the immediate clearance of ₹480 crore in long-pending dues for former Jet Airways staff. The ruling sets a strict two-week deadline for distribution following years of litigation and liquidation proceedings.
point1: NCLAT cleared ₹480 crore in back pay and benefits owed to former Jet Airways employees.
point2: The order addresses employee claims following the airline's 2019 grounding and 2024 liquidation.
point3: Funds are mandated to be disbursed within two weeks.

title: Indian government announces special Parliament sitting for Delimitation Bill
summary: The Indian government announced a special session of Parliament scheduled to take place from November 30 to December 3, 2026. Official statements indicate that the amended Delimitation Bill will be introduced during the four-day sitting.
point1: Parliament will reconvene for a special four-day session starting November 30.
point2: The sitting is designated for tabling and reviewing the amended Delimitation Bill.
point3: The special Parliament sitting will run from November 30 to December 3, 2026.

title: Nvidia pauses server chip shipments to Southeast Asian countries
summary: Nvidia instructed manufacturing partners to halt server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. The decision comes amid tightening U.S. regulatory efforts aimed at preventing advanced artificial intelligence chips from reaching China.
point1: Nvidia directed manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to four Southeast Asian nations.
point2: The move reflects escalating U.S. export controls intended to restrict China's access to high-end hardware.
point3: No confirmed timeline reported.
